questions.q: Who had the Mole long wanted to meet at the start of this chapter?
choices: The Badger
The Otter
Mr. Toad
The Rat's cousin
questions.evidence: The Mole had long wanted to make the acquaintance of the Badger.

questions.q: Why did the Rat say they could not invite the Badger to dinner?
choices: Badger hates Society, invitations and dinners
Badger was away on a long journey to the Wide World
Badger and the Rat had quarreled over Toad
Badger only ever eats alone at midnight
questions.evidence: Badger hates Society, and invitations, and dinner

questions.q: The Rat answered the Mole "evasively" about the Wild Wood. What does "evasively" mean?
choices: Avoiding giving a straight answer
Very loudly and rather angrily
Cheerfully and eagerly, with a smile
Slowly and sleepily, half awake

questions.q: What season was it when the Mole decided to go into the Wild Wood?
choices: Winter
Spring
Summer
Autumn
questions.evidence: In the winter time the Rat slept a great deal

questions.q: What was the Rat doing when the Mole slipped out of the house alone?
choices: Dozing by the fire and trying to write rhymes
Visiting Toad Hall to see how Toad was getting on
Out fishing on the river with the Otter
Cooking a hot supper in the kitchen
questions.evidence: alternately dozing and trying over rhymes that wouldn't fit

questions.q: What was the first frightening thing the Mole saw in the Wild Wood?
choices: Little evil faces looking out at him from holes
A huge red fox blocking the narrow path ahead
Glowing yellow eyes high up in the bare trees
A broken cart lying on its side in a ditch
questions.evidence: a little evil wedge-shaped face, looking out at him from a hole

questions.q: In what order did the frightening things happen to the Mole in the wood?
choices: The faces, then the whistling, then the pattering
The pattering, then the faces, then the whistling
The whistling, then the pattering, then the faces
The faces, then the pattering, then the whistling

questions.q: What did the rabbit say as it dashed past the Mole?
choices: 'Get out of this, you fool, get out!'
'Follow me, quickly, to somewhere safe!'
'Have you seen the Badger anywhere about?'
'Sixpence to pass along this way!'
questions.evidence: 'Get out of this, you fool, get out!'

questions.q: Where did the Mole hide when he was too tired to run any further?
choices: In the hollow of an old beech tree
Under a heap of mossy rocks and leaves
Deep inside an empty rabbit burrow
Behind a fallen log by a frozen stream
questions.evidence: he took refuge in the deep dark hollow of an old beech tree

questions.q: How did the Rat figure out where the Mole had gone?
choices: He followed the prints of Mole's new goloshes
The Otter told him he had seen the Mole go by
The Mole had left a note on the kitchen table
He heard the Mole calling to him from far away
questions.evidence: He could see the imprints of them in the mud

questions.q: What did the Rat take with him when he went to find the Mole?
choices: A brace of pistols and a stout cudgel
A lantern, a rope and a map of the wood
A basket of food and a warm blanket
A long rope and a heavy fishing net
questions.evidence: shoved a brace of pistols into it, took up a stout cudgel

questions.q: What did the Rat say river-bankers usually do if they must go into the Wild Wood?
choices: Go in pairs at least, and know the passwords
Go only at midnight, when the weasels are asleep
Go alone and very quietly, keeping to the paths
Take the Badger along to protect them the whole way
questions.evidence: If we have to come, we come in couples, at least

questions.q: What does the Rat say about whether Toad would come into the Wild Wood alone?
choices: Toad would never dare, not for a hatful of guineas
Toad comes there every week to visit his cousins
Toad is the bravest animal who goes in the wood
Toad often walks there alone on dark winter evenings
questions.evidence: He wouldn't show his face here alone, not for a whole hatful of golden guineas

questions.q: What did the Rat discover when he looked outside after the Mole's rest?
choices: It was snowing hard
The weasels had surrounded the tree
The sun was rising
The Badger was waiting outside

questions.q: What had the Mole tripped over and cut his shin on?
choices: A door-scraper hidden in the snow
A sharp rock hidden under the snow
A fallen branch from a beech tree
A broken bottle left by the weasels

questions.q: The Rat was "in despair at his obtuseness." What does "obtuseness" mean here?
choices: Being slow to understand something
Being very rude to a friend
Being badly hurt and bruised
Being far too noisy

questions.q: Why did the Rat get so excited about the door-scraper and the door-mat?
choices: He saw that a front door, and shelter, must be near
He wanted to carry them home as a gift for Toad Hall
He thought they could use the mat as a sled home
He liked to collect odd old things he found lying about
questions.evidence: that door exists, as plain as if I saw it

questions.q: What is this chapter mostly about?
choices: The Mole is lost in the Wild Wood until the Rat rescues him
The Mole and the Rat go on a long summer picnic by the river
Toad crashes his new motor-car into the Wild Wood
The Badger throws a winter party for all the animals
